item.title: Israel's election too close to call. And, the Ebola outbreak reaches grim milestone
item.description: Israeli voters turned out in record numbers, and the results remain too close to call. And, more than 10,000 people have been infected with Ebola since the outbreak was first declared in May.
item.content:encoded:
Israeli voters turned out in record numbers, and the results remain too close to call. And, more than 10,000 people have been infected with Ebola since the outbreak was first declared in May.

(Image credit: Maya Levin, Jewel Samad)

item.title: At least 30 dead in crash between two trains in central Spain, media say
item.description: A high-speed train slammed into the rear of another train that had stopped, derailing two cars and killing at least 30 people on Wednesday in central Spain, according to local media.
item.content:encoded:
A high-speed train slammed into the rear of another train that had stopped, derailing two cars and killing at least 30 people on Wednesday in central Spain, according to local media.

(Image credit: Juanma Jiménez)

item.description: President Trump's relationship with Russia's Vladimir Putin is under scrutiny again as the president makes deals with Moscow ahead of the midterms.

item.title: Partial results from Israel's contentious election show no clear winner
item.description: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing bloc was leading opposition rival Gadi Eisenkot. Arab parties had a strong showing, and a key question now is whether Eisenkot's bloc will consider forming a coalition with them.
item.content:encoded:

item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro leaves Brazil for the U.S. amid a money-laundering probe, as Washington agrees to issue visas to him and his family.

item.title: Israel's voter turnout soars as Netanyahu faces a tight election
item.description: Israelis voted in their highest numbers in over two decades in a tense national election to decide whether to stick with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's far-right coalition.

item.title: The Ebola outbreak is breaking records -- and just marked a grim milestone
item.description: The current outbreak, first identified in the Democratic Republic of Congo, has now counted 10,000 patients and has spread with great speed. How can it be stopped?

item.title: Bolsonaro's party accepts Brazil election defeat, but he refuses to concede
item.description: Brazil's opposition party accepts President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's election victory, but Flávio Bolsonaro won't concede, while President Trump calls the vote "rigged" without offering evidence.
